title: Bulk SMS for Events in Nigeria: How to Send Invitations and Reminders to Hundreds of Guests
excerpt: Learn how Nigerian event organisers can use bulk SMS for invitations, reminders and updates while keeping guest communication organised.
author: Ariya Journal
content:
Introduction

Organising an event involves more than choosing a venue, preparing a guest list and making arrangements for the day. One of the biggest challenges event organisers face is keeping guests informed before and during an event.

From sending invitations and registration confirmations to sharing reminders and important updates, communicating with hundreds or even thousands of guests can become difficult when handled manually.

Imagine having to send individual messages to 500 wedding guests or remind 1,000 conference attendees about an upcoming event. It would take considerable time and effort.

This is why many event organisers are turning to bulk SMS for events.

With AriyaHQ, organisers can manage important event activities, including guest invitations, registrations and communication, through one event management platform.

In this guide, we’ll explore how bulk SMS works for events, its benefits and how Ariya can help make event communication easier.

What Is Bulk SMS for Events?

Bulk SMS for events is the process of sending text messages to multiple recipients simultaneously.

Instead of sending individual messages to every guest, organisers can communicate with large groups of people through a bulk messaging service.

These messages can be used for:

  • Event invitations.
  • Registration confirmations.
  • RSVP reminders.
  • Event date reminders.
  • Venue and location updates.
  • Schedule changes.
  • Ticket and guest pass notifications.
  • Important event announcements.

For example, a wedding planner organising an event with 400 invited guests can use bulk SMS to communicate important information without manually sending hundreds of separate messages.

Bulk SMS is particularly useful for weddings, conferences, seminars, corporate events, church programmes and other large gatherings.

Why Is Bulk SMS Important for Event Organisers in Nigeria?

Event communication is especially important when guests are expected to travel, make arrangements or register before attending.

Here are some reasons bulk SMS can be valuable.

1. Reach Many Guests Quickly

Sending individual messages to hundreds of guests can be time-consuming.

Bulk SMS allows organisers to communicate with multiple recipients at once, helping them distribute important event information more efficiently.

2. Improve Event Attendance

Some guests may forget event dates or overlook invitation emails.

Sending reminders before the event helps keep the occasion on their minds and encourages them to make the necessary arrangements.

3. Share Important Event Updates

Event details can change during the planning process.

Organisers may need to communicate changes to the venue, event time, programme or other arrangements.

Bulk SMS provides a direct way to share important updates with guests.

4. Reduce Manual Communication

Without a proper communication system, event organisers may spend hours contacting guests individually.

Bulk messaging helps reduce repetitive communication tasks and makes it easier to reach large guest lists.

5. Improve the Guest Experience

Guests appreciate receiving clear and timely information.

Sending registration confirmations, reminders and relevant updates helps guests know what to expect and how to prepare.

How to Use Bulk SMS for Your Event

Bulk SMS can support different stages of event planning.

Here are some practical ways to use it.

1. Send Event Invitations

Use SMS to notify potential attendees about your upcoming event.

A simple invitation message should include the event name, date and a link to the registration or invitation page.

Example:

“You’re invited! Join us for the Annual Business Conference on 15 December 2026. Register here: [Registration Link]. We look forward to seeing you.”

2. Send Registration Confirmations

After guests register, send a confirmation message acknowledging their registration.

This reassures attendees that their details have been received.

Example:

“Your registration for the Annual Business Conference has been confirmed. We look forward to welcoming you. Further event details will be shared soon.”

3. Send Event Reminders

People have busy schedules, and invitations can easily be forgotten.

Send reminders a few days before the event and another closer to the event date.

Example:

“Just a reminder! Our Annual Business Conference takes place tomorrow at 10 AM. Venue: [Venue Details]. We look forward to seeing you.”

4. Share Venue and Location Information

Help guests find the event venue by sharing the address and directions.

You can also include a Google Maps link where appropriate.

5. Communicate Schedule Changes

If the event time, venue or programme changes, use SMS to notify registered guests as quickly as possible.

6. Share Guest Pass Information

For events that use digital tickets or QR code invitations, SMS can help communicate how guests can access their individual passes, provided the platform supports this delivery method.

How Ariya Helps You Manage Event Communication

Sending messages is only one part of event management.

Organisers also need to manage guest information, invitations, registrations, attendance and event updates.

AriyaHQ helps bring these important activities together through an event management platform designed for organisers.

Instead of relying entirely on separate tools and manual processes, organisers can use Ariya to manage different aspects of their events.

With Ariya, you can access tools for:

Digital Event Invitations: Create and manage invitations for weddings, corporate gatherings, celebrations and other events.

Guest Registration and RSVP: Organise guest responses and keep track of expected attendees.

Bulk SMS Communication: Use available messaging capabilities to communicate event information and updates to guests.

Bulk Email Communication: Reach guests through email for invitations, confirmations and other event-related information.

QR Code Guest Passes: Help organise guest identification and event access through digital passes.

Guest Management: Keep guest information organised and simplify event coordination.

The advantage is having a more connected event management process instead of handling every activity separately.

Start organising your event with Ariya to discover how you can simplify your event planning and guest communication.

Bulk SMS vs Bulk Email for Events: Which Is Better?

Both SMS and email are useful communication channels, but they serve slightly different purposes.

Feature Bulk SMS Bulk Email
Message format Short text messages Longer messages with rich content
Best for Quick updates and reminders Detailed invitations and announcements
Guest communication Direct messaging Detailed information delivery
Event reminders Useful for short reminders Useful for detailed reminders
Digital invitations Can share links Can include designed invitations
Ticket information Can share supported links Can deliver detailed ticket information

The best approach is not necessarily choosing one over the other.

Using SMS and email together can help event organisers communicate effectively at different stages of event planning.

For example, an organiser can send a detailed event invitation through email and follow up with an SMS reminder a few days before the event.

Best Bulk SMS Practices for Event Organisers

To get the most out of bulk SMS, consider the following practices.

Keep Messages Short and Clear

SMS messages have limited space. Focus on the most important information and avoid unnecessary wording.

Personalise Messages Where Possible

Addressing guests by their names can make communication feel more personal.

Include Important Event Details

Ensure messages contain relevant information such as the event date, time, venue and registration link.

Send Messages at Appropriate Times

Avoid sending event messages too early in the morning or too late at night.

Segment Your Guest List

Not every message needs to go to every guest.

For example, VIP guests may need different information from regular attendees.

Avoid Sending Unnecessary Messages

Communicate important updates without overwhelming guests with too many notifications.

Obtain Appropriate Consent

Ensure that guests have agreed to receive event-related communications and provide an appropriate way to manage communication preferences.

Bulk SMS Message Templates for Different Events

Here are some examples event organisers can adapt.

Wedding Invitation SMS

“You’re warmly invited to celebrate with us! Join us for [Names]’ wedding on [Date] at [Venue]. We look forward to celebrating this special day with you.”

Conference Registration Confirmation

“Your registration for [Conference Name] has been confirmed. Join us on [Date] at [Venue]. Thank you for registering!”

Event Reminder SMS

“Your event reminder! [Event Name] takes place tomorrow at [Time]. Venue: [Venue]. We look forward to welcoming you.”

Venue Update SMS

“Important update: The venue for [Event Name] has changed to [New Venue]. The event date and time remain unchanged. Thank you for your understanding.”

Birthday Celebration Invitation

“You’re invited to celebrate [Name]'s birthday! Join us on [Date] at [Venue]. We can’t wait to celebrate with you!”

These templates can be adapted to suit different event types and communication needs.

Who Needs Bulk SMS for Events?

Bulk SMS is useful for different types of event organisers.

Wedding Planners: Communicate wedding invitations, reminders and important updates to guests.

Corporate Event Organisers: Notify attendees about conferences, product launches, meetings and business gatherings.

Church Event Organisers: Share information about conventions, special programmes and church celebrations.

Conference Organisers: Communicate registration details, event reminders and programme updates.

Birthday and Private Event Hosts: Send invitations and reminders to friends, family members and other guests.

Event Management Companies: Manage communication across multiple events and large guest lists.

Frequently Asked Questions About Bulk SMS for Events

The best approach is to use a bulk messaging or event management platform that allows you to organise your recipients and distribute messages efficiently. AriyaHQ offers event communication capabilities as part of its broader event management solution.

Can I send SMS invitations to hundreds of guests?

Yes. Bulk SMS services allow organisers to send messages to multiple recipients simultaneously, subject to the provider’s sending limits and available messaging credits.

Can I use bulk SMS for wedding invitations?

Yes. Bulk SMS can be used to notify guests about wedding celebrations, share invitation links and send important reminders.

Can bulk SMS be used to send event reminders?

Absolutely. Organisers can send reminders before an event to help guests remember the date, time and venue.

Is bulk SMS better than email for event communication?

Both have different advantages. SMS is useful for short and timely updates, while email is better for detailed invitations and information. Using both channels can provide a more complete communication strategy.

Can I send QR code tickets through SMS?

This depends on the platform. Some systems allow organisers to send ticket links or QR code information through SMS, while others use email or dedicated digital passes.

How much does bulk SMS cost in Nigeria?

Bulk SMS pricing varies depending on the provider, network, message length and number of recipients. Organisers should compare available pricing and delivery options before choosing a service.

From invitations and registration to guest communication and event access, having the right tools can make the entire process easier.

AriyaHQ helps event organisers bring important event management activities together, making it easier to organise guests, communicate event information and coordinate successful events.

What Is Bulk Email for Events?

Bulk email for events is the process of sending one email campaign to multiple recipients simultaneously.

Instead of composing and sending individual emails to every guest, organisers can distribute event-related information to an entire mailing list or selected groups of recipients.

Bulk emails can be used for:

  • Event invitations.
  • Registration confirmations.
  • Event announcements.
  • RSVP reminders.
  • Programme updates.
  • Venue and schedule changes.
  • Ticket information.
  • Post-event appreciation messages.

For example, a conference organiser can send an invitation to 1,000 potential attendees using a bulk email platform instead of contacting each person individually.

This makes communication more organised and helps ensure that guests receive consistent information.

Why Should Event Organisers Use Bulk Email?

Bulk email offers several advantages, particularly when managing events with large guest lists.

1. Reach Hundreds or Thousands of Guests

Bulk email makes it easier to distribute information to large groups of people without sending messages individually.

This is particularly useful for conferences, corporate events, weddings and public gatherings.

2. Send Detailed Event Invitations

Unlike SMS, email allows organisers to include more information in a single message.

You can provide:

  • Event descriptions.
  • Date and time.
  • Venue information.
  • Event schedules.
  • Registration links.
  • Images and branded designs.
  • Additional instructions.

This makes email particularly useful for formal invitations and detailed event announcements.

3. Automate Important Communication

Depending on the platform, event organisers can automate messages such as registration confirmations and scheduled reminders.

This reduces repetitive administrative work and helps guests receive important information at the right time.

4. Keep Guests Updated

Event details can change during the planning process.

Bulk email makes it easier to notify registered attendees about programme changes, new instructions, venue updates and other important announcements.

5. Maintain Professional Communication

A properly designed event email creates a more professional impression.

Organisers can use branded email templates, consistent messaging and clear calls to action to communicate effectively.

Types of Emails Every Event Organiser Should Send

A successful event communication strategy involves more than sending one invitation.

Here are some important emails to consider throughout the event planning process.

1. Event Announcement Emails

This is usually the first communication potential attendees receive.

It introduces the event and provides the essential information people need to decide whether they want to attend.

Include:

  • Event name.
  • Date and time.
  • Venue.
  • Main event highlights.
  • Registration link.

Example:

Subject: You’re Invited to Our Annual Business Conference!

Hello [Guest Name],

We’re excited to invite you to our Annual Business Conference, bringing together business leaders, professionals and entrepreneurs for an engaging experience.

Date: 15 December 2026
Time: 10:00 AM
Venue: [Event Venue]

Secure your place by registering here: [Registration Link].

We look forward to welcoming you!

2. Registration Confirmation Emails

After someone registers for your event, send a confirmation email acknowledging their registration.

This reassures attendees that their registration was successful.

Example:

Subject: Your Event Registration Is Confirmed!

Hello [Guest Name],

Thank you for registering for [Event Name].

Your registration has been received successfully. We look forward to having you join us.

Event Date: [Date]
Venue: [Venue]

Keep an eye on your inbox for further event information.

3. Event Reminder Emails

People have busy schedules, and it is easy to forget an upcoming event.

Send reminders a few days before the event and closer to the event date.

Example:

Subject: A Reminder About [Event Name]

Hello [Guest Name],

This is a friendly reminder that [Event Name] is happening soon!

Date: [Date]
Time: [Time]
Venue: [Venue]

We look forward to seeing you.

4. Event Programme Emails

For conferences, seminars and corporate gatherings, attendees may need detailed programme information.

Use email to share:

  • Session schedules.
  • Speaker information.
  • Workshop details.
  • Break times.
  • Special announcements.

5. Venue and Location Update Emails

If the event venue or schedule changes, notify registered attendees as soon as possible.

Make the updated information clear so guests do not rely on outdated invitations.

6. Post-Event Thank You Emails

Communication shouldn’t necessarily end when the event does.

Send appreciation messages to attendees, speakers, sponsors and other participants.

You can also include feedback forms, photographs and information about future events.

For example, VIP guests, registered attendees, speakers and sponsors may need different information.

Selling tickets is one of the most important parts of organising a successful event. Whether you’re planning a concert, conference, wedding, seminar or networking event, you need a reliable way to make tickets available to your audience and manage the people who intend to attend.

Today, you can sell event tickets online, receive registrations digitally and manage attendee information without depending entirely on manual processes.

With AriyaHQ, event organisers can manage important parts of their events, including digital invitations, guest registration, RSVP management and guest communication, through one platform.

In this guide, we’ll explain how online event ticketing works in Nigeria, what you need to get started and how to choose the right platform for your event.

What Does It Mean to Sell Event Tickets Online?

Selling event tickets online means making tickets available to attendees through a digital platform rather than relying only on physical sales or manual registration.

People can access an event’s registration or ticketing page, provide the required information and complete the purchase or registration process supported by the platform.

Depending on the ticketing system, attendees may receive digital tickets or confirmation details after registering.

For event organisers, this provides a more structured way to manage ticket sales, registrations and attendee information.

Why Should You Sell Event Tickets Online?

Online ticketing offers several advantages for event organisers.

1. Reach More Potential Attendees

With online ticketing, people can discover and register for your event from different locations without visiting a physical sales point.

You can share your event registration or ticket link through social media, email, WhatsApp and other marketing channels.

2. Make Registration More Convenient

Attendees can access your event information and complete registration online.

This removes the need for many guests to contact the organiser individually just to find out how to attend.

3. Manage Attendee Information

Instead of keeping separate paper lists or manually combining registration details, an online platform can help organise attendee information digitally.

This makes it easier to review registrations and prepare for the event.

4. Promote Different Ticket Categories

Some events offer multiple ticket options, such as:

  • Regular tickets.
  • VIP tickets.
  • Early-bird tickets.

A suitable ticketing platform can help organisers present different ticket categories to their audience.

5. Simplify Event Communication

Once people register, organisers need to communicate important information such as event dates, venue details, reminders and changes.

6. Improve Event Preparation

Having registration information available before the event helps organisers estimate attendance and prepare resources accordingly.

How to Sell Event Tickets Online in Nigeria

Step 1: Decide on Your Ticket Types

Before choosing a platform, determine the types of tickets you want to offer.

For example, a conference could have regular and VIP tickets, while a concert could offer early-bird, regular and premium access options.

Consider your audience, event budget and the experience you want attendees to have.

Step 2: Set Your Ticket Prices

Your ticket price should reflect the value of the experience you’re offering while accounting for event expenses.

Consider costs such as:

  • Venue rental.
  • Decorations and production.
  • Entertainment.
  • Catering.
  • Marketing.
  • Staff and logistics.
  • Payment processing fees.
  • Ticketing platform charges.

If you offer different ticket categories, ensure that each price has a clear justification.

Step 3: Choose an Online Ticketing Platform

You need a platform that can support the ticketing or registration process required for your event.

When comparing platforms, consider:

  • Ease of event creation.
  • Ticket category management.
  • Online registration.
  • Payment collection options.
  • Attendee information management.
  • Digital ticket delivery.
  • Guest verification and check-in.
  • Customer support.

If you’re also managing invitations and guest communication, consider an event management platform that brings these activities together.

Step 4: Create Your Event Page

Your event page should provide all the information potential attendees need before registering.

Include:

  • Event name.
  • Event description.
  • Date and time.
  • Venue or location.
  • Ticket categories.
  • Ticket prices.
  • Registration instructions.
  • Contact information.
  • Terms and conditions, where applicable.

Use clear descriptions and attractive event images to help people understand what they’re registering for.

Step 5: Make Tickets Available

Once your event page and ticket options are ready, publish or share the registration link with your audience.

Make it easy for people to understand which ticket they should choose and how to complete registration.

Step 6: Promote Your Event

Creating tickets is only one part of selling them. You also need to make potential attendees aware of your event.

Promote your event through:

  • Instagram.
  • Facebook.
  • X (Twitter).
  • WhatsApp.
  • Email newsletters.
  • Influencer partnerships.
  • Event communities.
  • Your website.

You can also encourage registered attendees to share the event with friends and colleagues.

Step 7: Manage Registrations and Attendees

As people register, keep track of attendee information and prepare for the event.

Organise your guest records, communicate important updates and make sure your team knows how to verify attendees when they arrive.

Step 8: Prepare for Event-Day Check-in

Before the event, decide how attendees will be admitted.

Prepare your registration team and test the process before guests begin arriving.

Introduction

You can spend months planning an event, book an impressive venue, invite great speakers or performers and organise everything down to the smallest detail. But if people don’t know about the event, getting the attendance you want becomes difficult.

Event promotion is one of the most important parts of organising a successful event. It determines how many people discover your event, how interested they become and whether they eventually register or buy a ticket.

In Nigeria, promoting an event requires more than designing a flyer and posting it on Instagram. You need a deliberate strategy that combines social media, WhatsApp, email, SMS, partnerships, word of mouth and, where appropriate, paid advertising.

You also need a way to manage the people who respond to your marketing.

This is where AriyaHQ can support your event operations. While your marketing channels attract potential attendees, Ariya helps you manage important activities such as digital invitations, guest registration, RSVP responses and communication.

Whether you’re promoting a concert in Lagos, a conference in Abuja, a wedding in Ibadan or a corporate event in Port Harcourt, this guide will show you how to build an event promotion strategy that gives your event a better chance of attracting attendees.

1. Start by Understanding Who You Want to Attend

Before spending money on advertising or creating promotional content, define your target audience.

One of the biggest mistakes event organisers make is trying to promote an event to everybody.

Not everyone will be interested in your event, and promoting to the wrong audience wastes time and money.

Start by answering these questions:

  • Who is the event designed for?
  • Where do potential attendees live?
  • What age group are you targeting?
  • What interests or problems would make them attend?
  • How much are they willing to spend?
  • Which platforms do they use?
  • What would convince them that your event is worth attending?

For example, consider these three events:

Event Likely target audience Promotional angle
Business conference in Lagos Entrepreneurs, executives and professionals Networking, business growth and industry insights
Music concert in Abuja Music lovers and entertainment audiences Performers, atmosphere and live entertainment
Wedding exhibition in Ibadan Engaged couples and wedding vendors Wedding inspiration, vendors and planning resources

Your promotional message should reflect what matters to the people you’re trying to reach.

A business conference should not be marketed in exactly the same way as a music concert.

2. Create a Strong Event Marketing Message

Before promoting your event, you need to communicate why people should attend.

A flyer containing only the event name, date and venue may provide basic information, but it does not necessarily give someone a reason to register.

Your marketing message should answer three questions:

What is happening? Explain what the event is about.

Who should attend? Help potential attendees recognise that the event is relevant to them.

Why should they attend? Communicate the value or experience they will get.

For example, instead of writing:

“Business Growth Conference 2027. Lagos. Register now.”

Try something more specific:

“Ready to grow your business beyond referrals? Join entrepreneurs, business leaders and industry experts in Lagos for practical conversations on building profitable businesses.”

The second message gives people a clearer reason to pay attention.

Your event’s promotional message should remain consistent across your website, social media posts, advertisements, emails and WhatsApp messages.

3. Use the Right Platforms to Promote Your Event in Nigeria

You don’t need to be everywhere. You need to be visible where your potential attendees spend their time.

A 2024 PwC survey of Nigerian MSMEs identified WhatsApp Business, Facebook and Instagram among the digital channels businesses use, alongside email marketing and bulk SMS. These figures describe business channel usage rather than event attendance or advertising effectiveness, but they illustrate why a multi-channel approach is worth considering. Source: PwC Nigeria MSME Survey.

Here is how to approach the major channels.

Instagram: Build Interest Through Visual Content

Instagram is useful for events where images, videos, personalities and experiences influence people’s decisions.

Use it to:

  • Publish your official event announcement.
  • Introduce speakers, performers and special guests.
  • Share behind-the-scenes preparation.
  • Publish short videos explaining what attendees should expect.
  • Share testimonials from previous editions.
  • Post countdowns as the event approaches.
  • Collaborate with relevant creators.

Don’t make every post a sales announcement.

Mix promotional content with material that gives people a reason to become interested in the event.

TikTok: Create Discovery Through Short Videos

TikTok can help events reach people who have not previously heard about them.

Rather than posting only a digital flyer, create short videos that communicate the event’s appeal.

Examples include:

  • A speaker explaining one thing attendees will learn.
  • A performer inviting fans to the event.
  • A behind-the-scenes look at preparations.
  • A short preview of the venue.
  • A video answering common attendee questions.
  • Highlights from a previous edition.

The goal is to make people curious enough to visit your event page or ask for more information.

Facebook: Reach Communities and Interest Groups

Facebook can be useful for reaching community groups, professional audiences and people interested in particular event categories.

Consider:

  • Sharing your event on your organisation’s page.
  • Publishing relevant updates in appropriate groups, subject to group rules.
  • Running targeted advertisements.
  • Encouraging partners and speakers to share the event.
  • Using event-related discussions to answer questions.

Avoid posting promotional links indiscriminately in unrelated groups. Focus on communities where your event is genuinely relevant.

WhatsApp: Turn Personal Recommendations into Registrations

WhatsApp is particularly useful for direct event communication in Nigeria.

You can use it to:

  • Share event announcements with relevant contacts.
  • Distribute promotional graphics and videos.
  • Send registration links.
  • Provide answers to questions.
  • Share updates with interested attendees.
  • Encourage previous attendees to recommend the event.

WhatsApp Status can also help keep your event visible to people who already know you.

However, avoid adding people to groups without their permission or sending repeated unsolicited promotional messages. Respect people’s communication preferences.

X: Build Conversations Around Your Event

X can be useful for conferences, technology events, public discussions, professional gatherings and events involving active online communities.

Try:

  • Announcing speakers and programme highlights.
  • Publishing discussion topics.
  • Sharing short updates from organisers.
  • Engaging with relevant industry conversations.
  • Encouraging speakers and partners to participate in event discussions.

A useful approach is to give people something interesting to discuss rather than simply repeating the registration link.

LinkedIn: Promote Professional and Corporate Events

For business conferences, executive gatherings, workshops and networking events, LinkedIn can help you reach relevant professional audiences.

Ask speakers, sponsors and participating organisations to share the event with their professional networks.

Focus your messaging on the business value of attending.

4. Build a Promotion Timeline Instead of Posting Randomly

A successful event campaign should have different stages.

Posting the same flyer every few days is not a marketing strategy.

Your audience needs to discover the event, understand its value, consider attending and eventually take action.

Here is a practical eight-week promotion timeline.

Period Main objective What to do
8 weeks before Awareness Announce the event and publish the official event information
7 weeks before Discovery Introduce the event concept and target audience
6 weeks before Interest Reveal speakers, performers, partners or programme highlights
5 weeks before Consideration Publish useful content explaining why people should attend
4 weeks before Conversion Increase registration and ticket promotion
3 weeks before Social proof Share testimonials, previous event highlights and endorsements
2 weeks before Urgency Communicate genuine deadlines and remaining ticket availability
Final week Attendance preparation Send relevant reminders, venue details and entry instructions

For events with shorter planning periods, compress the schedule. The important thing is to give each stage a purpose.

5. Create Content That Sells the Experience, Not Just the Event

People don’t attend events simply because they see a flyer. They attend because they believe the experience will be worth their time and money.

Your content should communicate that value.

Here are some content ideas you can use.

The Announcement Post

Introduce the event and communicate the most important details.

Include the event name, date, venue, central theme and registration information.

The Speaker or Performer Reveal

Introduce the people who will make the event interesting.

Share short biographies, previous work, achievements or a video invitation.

The Behind-the-Scenes Post

Show the preparation happening before the event.

This helps make the event feel real and gives people a reason to follow the journey.

The Educational Post

For conferences and workshops, share useful information related to the event’s subject.

For example, a business conference could publish short tips about customer acquisition, financial management or business growth.

The Testimonial Post

If the event has previous editions, use genuine feedback and photographs from attendees.

Social proof can help potential attendees understand what to expect.

The Frequently Asked Questions Post

Answer common questions about:

  • Ticket prices.
  • Venue location.
  • Parking.
  • Dress code.
  • Event schedule.
  • Age restrictions, if applicable.
  • Registration and entry requirements.

The Countdown Post

As the event approaches, remind people about the date and any genuine registration deadlines.

Give each countdown post a different angle rather than simply changing the number of days remaining.

6. Use Influencers, Speakers and Brand Partners to Expand Your Reach

You don’t have to promote an event entirely through your own social media accounts.

Other people and organisations may already have access to the audience you want to reach.

Consider working with:

Influencers and Content Creators: Identify creators whose audiences match your target attendees. A smaller creator with a relevant audience may be more useful than a large account with an unrelated following.

Speakers and Performers: Ask confirmed speakers and performers to share the event with their own audiences.

Sponsors: Give sponsors promotional materials and clear instructions on how to communicate their involvement.

Media Partners: Collaborate with relevant blogs, publications, radio stations or entertainment platforms.

Community Leaders: For specialised events, connect with associations, professional groups and relevant communities.

When working with influencers, agree on deliverables before the campaign starts.

Specify the number of posts, publication dates, content format, registration link and how results will be measured.

Don’t judge a partnership only by the number of followers. Look at audience relevance, engagement and actual registrations generated.

7. Run Paid Advertisements Strategically

Paid advertising can help your event reach people beyond your existing audience.

However, spending money on advertisements without a clear strategy can quickly consume your budget.

Start by deciding what action you want people to take.

For example:

  • Visit your event page.
  • Register for the event.
  • Purchase a ticket.
  • Send an enquiry.
  • Join an event mailing list.

Then select an advertising channel that supports your objective.

Meta Ads: Facebook and Instagram

Meta advertising can help you reach audiences based on available targeting options and promote event content across Facebook and Instagram.

You can test different creatives, audiences and messages to understand what generates the most meaningful response.

TikTok Ads

TikTok advertisements may be suitable for events that can be promoted effectively through short-form video.

Use creative content that feels natural to the platform.

Google Ads

Google Search advertising can help reach people actively searching for relevant events, conferences, workshops or experiences.

For example, an organiser promoting a business conference could target relevant searches around business conferences in Lagos.

Start with a Test Budget

Rather than spending your entire advertising budget immediately, start with a controlled test.

Compare:

  • Different audiences.
  • Different creative formats.
  • Different promotional messages.
  • Different registration landing pages.

Increase spending on campaigns that produce meaningful results, not simply those with the most likes or views.

8. Give People a Clear Way to Register

Imagine someone sees your event advertisement, becomes interested and decides to attend.

What happens next?

If they have to send several messages, wait for a response, request payment details and manually confirm their registration, you may lose some interested attendees along the way.

Your registration process should be simple.

Make sure potential attendees can easily find:

  • The official event information.
  • The registration or ticket link.
  • Available ticket options, if applicable.
  • Payment instructions, where applicable.
  • Confirmation details.
  • Contact information for enquiries.

This is also where event management software becomes useful.

AriyaHQ helps organisers manage the event journey after promotion, with tools for digital invitations, guest registration, RSVP management, QR code guest passes and guest communication.

You can use your social media campaigns, partnerships and advertising to attract attention, then direct interested people towards the appropriate Ariya-supported invitation or registration process.

Explore Create your event on Ariya to see how it can support the organisation of your event.

9. Use SMS and Email to Follow Up with Interested Attendees

Your promotional campaign should not end when someone registers or expresses interest.

People may forget event dates, overlook important information or need reminders before making final arrangements.

Email and SMS can help you maintain communication.

What to Send Through Email

Email is useful for messages that require more information or presentation.

Examples include:

  • Formal event announcements.
  • Registration confirmations.
  • Speaker and programme updates.
  • Detailed event instructions.
  • Important changes to the event.

What to Send Through SMS

SMS is useful for short, direct messages.

Examples include:

  • Registration reminders.
  • Event date reminders.
  • Venue changes.
  • Time-sensitive announcements.
  • Entry instructions.

For example:

Event reminder:

“Your event is almost here! Join us this Saturday at 10 AM at [Venue]. Please arrive early and have your registration confirmation ready. We look forward to seeing you.”

Use these channels responsibly. Send messages to people who have provided their contact details for relevant event communication, and provide an appropriate way to opt out of promotional messages.

With Ariya’s bulk SMS and email capabilities, organisers can manage important guest communication alongside their event activities.

10. Track the Numbers That Actually Matter

A campaign can receive thousands of views and still produce very few registrations.

This is why event organisers should measure outcomes rather than focusing only on social media engagement.

Here are some useful metrics.

Metric What it tells you
Reach How many accounts saw your promotional content
Engagement How people interacted with your content
Link clicks How many people visited your registration page
Registrations How many people completed registration
Ticket sales How many paid tickets were purchased
Cost per registration How much you spent to generate each registration
Attendance rate How many registered attendees actually attended

For example, imagine you spend ₦100,000 promoting an event and generate 200 registrations.

Your cost per registration is:

₦100,000 ÷ 200 = ₦500 per registration.

This does not automatically mean the campaign is profitable. You still need to consider ticket revenue, event costs, cancellations and actual attendance.

Use tracking links or campaign-specific codes to understand which channels generate results.

For example, you could create separate tracking links for Instagram, WhatsApp, influencer campaigns and paid advertisements.

This makes it easier to identify where your registrations are coming from.

11. Common Event Promotion Mistakes to Avoid

Even well-planned campaigns can underperform when organisers make avoidable mistakes.

Promoting Too Late: Give people enough time to discover the event, make plans and register.

Using Only Flyers: Flyers communicate information, but videos, testimonials, speaker introductions and useful content can create more interest.

Targeting Everyone: Focus your campaign on people who are genuinely likely to attend.

Ignoring Follow-ups: People may need reminders and additional information before completing registration.

Making Registration Difficult: Too many steps can discourage interested attendees.

Using Unclear Promotional Messages: Explain what the event offers and why someone should attend.

Spending on Ads Without Tracking Results: Measure registrations and ticket sales, not just views and likes.

Failing to Communicate After Registration: Keep attendees informed so they know what to expect and when to arrive.

A Practical Event Promotion Checklist

Use this checklist when preparing your next event campaign.

Before promotion

  • Define the target audience.
  • Establish the event’s main selling point.
  • Prepare the official event information.
  • Set up the registration or ticketing process.
  • Prepare promotional graphics and videos.
  • Create a marketing timeline.

During promotion

  • Publish the official announcement.
  • Introduce speakers, performers or special guests.
  • Share behind-the-scenes content.
  • Promote through relevant social platforms.
  • Activate influencers and partners.
  • Run and monitor paid campaigns where appropriate.
  • Track registrations and ticket sales.
  • Send relevant updates and reminders.

Before event day

  • Send final attendee information.
  • Confirm venue and programme details.
  • Prepare guest passes or tickets.
  • Organise the check-in team.
  • Communicate any last-minute changes.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I promote an event in Nigeria?

Start by identifying your target audience, developing a clear promotional message and choosing suitable channels. Use social media, WhatsApp, email, SMS, partnerships, influencers and paid advertising where appropriate. Give people a straightforward way to register and track the results of your campaigns.

There is no single best platform for every event. How early should I start promoting an event?

Should I use influencers to promote my event?

Introduction

Planning a corporate event involves more than booking a venue and inviting guests. Whether you are organising a conference, product launch, company anniversary, annual general meeting, business seminar or awards ceremony, every detail needs to come together to create a professional experience.

A successful corporate event requires proper budgeting, venue selection, guest management, communication, programme coordination and careful execution.

For organisations managing large guest lists, AriyaHQ can help simplify the process by bringing event invitations, registration, RSVP management, guest communication and check-in into one platform.

This checklist will guide you through the important stages of planning a corporate event in Nigeria, from the initial idea to the day the event takes place.

1. Define the Purpose of the Event

Before making bookings or contacting vendors, establish exactly why the organisation is hosting the event.

Your event objectives will influence almost every decision, including the venue, budget, programme, guest list and promotional strategy.

Common corporate event objectives include:

  • Brand awareness: Introducing a company, product or service to a wider audience.
  • Networking: Connecting professionals, business owners, investors or industry leaders.
  • Employee engagement: Bringing employees together for team-building, celebrations or internal communication.
  • Knowledge sharing: Hosting conferences, workshops, seminars or training sessions.
  • Business development: Building relationships with potential customers, partners and investors.
  • Recognition: Celebrating employees, partners, customers or business achievements.

Write down the main objective and identify what a successful event should achieve.

For example, if you are organising a product launch, success might mean attracting 200 invited guests, securing media coverage and generating qualified business enquiries.

2. Establish Your Event Budget

Your budget determines what you can realistically deliver. It is important to estimate costs before committing to vendors or announcing the event.

Use the following categories when preparing your budget.

Budget category What to consider
Venue Hall rental, conference facilities and venue deposits
Catering Meals, drinks, refreshments and service staff
Branding and decoration Stage design, banners, backdrops and branded materials
Audio-visual Projectors, screens, microphones, lighting and sound
Speakers and entertainment Speaker fees, performers, hosts and moderators
Marketing and communication Advertising, invitations, email and SMS
Registration and guest management Registration tools, badges, tickets and check-in
Logistics Transportation, accommodation and equipment movement
Photography and media Photographers, videographers and content coverage
Security and operations Security personnel, ushers and event support
Contingency Unexpected expenses and last-minute changes

Practical tip: Keep a contingency allowance in your budget. Unexpected costs can arise from additional guests, transportation changes, equipment issues or vendor adjustments.

Also, distinguish between estimated costs, confirmed costs and payments already made. This makes it easier to monitor spending throughout the planning process.

3. Choose the Right Event Date and Venue

The venue should match the nature of the event, the expected number of attendees and the experience you want to create.

When choosing a date in Nigeria, consider:

  • Public holidays and major religious celebrations.
  • Other industry events that may attract the same audience.
  • Traffic conditions and accessibility.
  • Availability of important speakers and executives.
  • Weather conditions, particularly for outdoor events.

When inspecting a venue, check the following:

  • Capacity and seating arrangements.
  • Location and accessibility.
  • Parking availability.
  • Electricity supply and backup power.
  • Air conditioning and ventilation.
  • Restrooms and other facilities.
  • Internet connectivity.
  • Stage, lighting and sound facilities.
  • Catering arrangements.
  • Security and emergency access.
  • Setup and breakdown times.

Do not choose a venue based on appearance alone. A beautiful venue that cannot comfortably accommodate your guests or support your event programme may create unnecessary problems.

4. Identify Your Target Audience and Prepare the Guest List

Your guest list should reflect the purpose of the event.

Depending on the event, your audience may include:

  • Company executives and employees.
  • Customers and prospective customers.
  • Business partners and investors.
  • Industry professionals.
  • Government representatives.
  • Media organisations.
  • Speakers, facilitators and special guests.

Create a structured guest list containing relevant information such as:

  • Full name.
  • Email address.
  • Phone number.
  • Organisation or company.
  • Guest category.
  • Invitation status.
  • Registration status.
  • Attendance confirmation.

For larger events, avoid managing multiple versions of the guest list across spreadsheets, email conversations and messaging applications.

A centralised guest management process makes it easier to track invitations, confirmations and expected attendance.

5. Set Up Event Invitations and Registration

Once the guest list and event details are ready, establish how people will receive invitations and confirm their attendance.

For formal corporate events, your invitation should clearly communicate:

  • Event name.
  • Date and time.
  • Venue or location.
  • Purpose of the event.
  • Key speakers or programme highlights, where applicable.
  • Registration instructions.
  • RSVP deadline.
  • Contact information for enquiries.

For events involving many guests, digital invitations and online registration can reduce the administrative work involved in collecting responses.

AriyaHQ helps organisers manage this process through digital event invitations, online registration and RSVP management. Instead of relying entirely on manual responses, organisers can use a more organised process to collect guest information and monitor attendance confirmations.

You can explore Explore Ariya for event teams to manage the guest registration and invitation side of your event.

6. Plan Your Event Programme

A corporate event should have a clear programme that keeps the event organised and ensures that important activities happen at the right time.

Depending on the type of event, your programme may include:

  • Guest arrival and registration.
  • Welcome address.
  • Opening remarks.
  • Keynote presentation.
  • Panel discussions.
  • Product demonstrations.
  • Networking sessions.
  • Refreshment breaks.
  • Awards or recognition.
  • Closing remarks.

Prepare a detailed running order showing the activity, responsible person and allocated time.

For example:

Time Activity
9:00 AM Guest arrival and registration
9:30 AM Opening remarks
9:45 AM Welcome address
10:00 AM Keynote presentation
10:45 AM Panel discussion
11:30 AM Refreshment and networking
12:00 PM Main presentation
1:00 PM Closing remarks

Share the programme with speakers, moderators, vendors and the internal event team before the event.

Allow reasonable flexibility for transitions, late arrivals and questions from attendees.

7. Confirm Speakers, Vendors and Event Partners

Your vendors and event partners play an important role in delivering the experience you have planned.

Depending on the event, you may need:

  • Event planners or coordinators.
  • Caterers.
  • Photographers and videographers.
  • Sound and lighting technicians.
  • Decorators and branding teams.
  • Hosts and moderators.
  • Security personnel.
  • Ushers and registration assistants.
  • Transportation providers.

For each vendor, confirm:

  1. The agreed service and deliverables.
  2. The total cost and payment schedule.
  3. Setup and delivery times.
  4. The person responsible for coordination.
  5. What happens if the vendor cannot deliver.
  6. Any additional costs that may arise.

Keep written records of important agreements. Do not rely solely on verbal arrangements, especially when dealing with significant event expenses.

8. Develop Your Event Communication Plan

Inviting guests is only one part of event communication. You also need to keep attendees informed before the event.

A simple communication schedule might look like this:

Timing Communication
When invitations are released Initial event invitation
After registration Registration confirmation
Two weeks before Event information and programme update
One week before Attendance reminder
One day before Final reminder with venue and arrival details
Event day Important announcements and updates
After the event Appreciation message and feedback request

For events with hundreds or thousands of attendees, sending individual messages manually can become difficult.

AriyaHQ supports event communication through bulk SMS and bulk email, helping organisers communicate event information and reminders to larger guest lists.

The key is to send relevant messages at the right time. Avoid overwhelming guests with unnecessary updates.

9. Organise Guest Passes and Event Check-in

Guest arrival is one of the first direct experiences attendees have with your event.

Poorly organised registration can result in long queues, confusion and delays, especially when many guests arrive around the same time.

For larger corporate events, consider using digital guest passes or QR code tickets.

A well-organised check-in process should include:

  • A prepared list of registered guests.
  • Clear registration points.
  • Trained registration personnel.
  • A process for verifying guest details.
  • A way to identify special guests and VIP attendees.
  • A process for handling guests who cannot find their registration details.
  • Clear directions to the event hall.

With AriyaHQ, organisers can use unique QR code guest passes to support guest identification and event entry management.

Before the event, test the check-in process with your registration team. Make sure everyone understands how guests will be verified and directed into the venue.

10. Prepare Your Event Team

Even with good planning, an event can become disorganised if nobody knows who is responsible for each activity.

Assign clear responsibilities before event day.

A basic corporate event team may include:

Role Responsibility
Event coordinator Oversees the entire event
Venue manager Handles venue arrangements
Guest registration team Manages guest arrival and check-in
Technical team Handles sound, lighting and presentations
Programme coordinator Ensures activities follow the schedule
Guest relations team Assists speakers, VIPs and attendees
Media team Handles photography, video and coverage
Logistics team Coordinates equipment and vendor movement

Hold a briefing before the event so that everyone understands their responsibilities, reporting lines and emergency contacts.

11. Conduct a Final Event Readiness Check

At least one or two days before the event, review every major arrangement.

Use this final checklist:

Venue and Logistics

  • Venue booking confirmed.
  • Seating arrangements completed.
  • Power supply and backup confirmed.
  • Sound and lighting tested.
  • Projectors and presentation equipment tested.
  • Directional signs and branding installed.

Guests and Registration

  • Guest list updated.
  • Invitations sent.
  • Registrations reviewed.
  • RSVP responses checked.
  • QR guest passes prepared where applicable.
  • Registration team briefed.

Programme and Vendors

  • Event programme finalised.
  • Speakers confirmed.
  • Vendors reconfirmed.
  • Presentation materials collected.
  • Host and moderators briefed.

Communication

  • Reminder messages prepared.
  • Venue directions shared.
  • Important contact details available.
  • Event team communication channel established.

This final review helps identify problems while there is still time to resolve them.

12. Manage the Event on the Day

On event day, the focus should shift from planning to execution.

The event coordinator should arrive early enough to inspect the venue, meet vendors and confirm that all teams are ready.

Pay particular attention to:

  • Registration and guest arrival.
  • Speaker arrival and preparation.
  • Programme timing.
  • Technical performance.
  • Catering and refreshments.
  • VIP and special guest arrangements.
  • Communication between event teams.
  • Unexpected changes or emergencies.

Keep one person responsible for making operational decisions. Too many people giving conflicting instructions can create confusion.

It is also important to document the event through photography, video and other media. These materials can support future marketing, internal reports and subsequent events.

13. Follow Up After the Event

An event does not end when the last guest leaves.

Post-event communication helps maintain relationships and gives your organisation an opportunity to measure the success of the event.

After the event:

  1. Send appreciation messages to attendees, speakers and partners.
  2. Share relevant photographs, recordings or presentation materials.
  3. Request feedback from attendees.
  4. Review attendance against registrations.
  5. Document expenses and compare them with the original budget.
  6. Evaluate whether the event achieved its objectives.
  7. Record lessons for future events.

For business-focused events, you may also need to follow up with prospective customers, partners or investors who attended.

Common Corporate Event Planning Mistakes to Avoid

Even experienced organisations can encounter problems when important details are overlooked.

Starting too late: Venues, speakers and reliable vendors may become unavailable if planning begins too close to the event date.

Underestimating the budget: Small expenses can accumulate and push the event beyond its approved budget.

Poor guest management: An unorganised guest list makes it difficult to track invitations, confirmations and attendance.

Ignoring event communication: Guests need timely information about the event, including reminders, directions and programme updates.

Failing to test equipment: Microphones, projectors, internet connections and presentation equipment should be tested before guests arrive.

Not assigning responsibilities: Every important task should have a clearly identified person responsible for it.

Ignoring post-event follow-up: Failing to communicate with attendees after the event means missing an opportunity to maintain valuable relationships.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I plan a corporate event in Nigeria?

Start by defining the purpose of the event, setting a budget, selecting a date and venue, preparing your guest list, arranging vendors, planning the programme and organising registration. You should also establish a communication plan and prepare an event-day team.

How early should you start planning a corporate event?

For a small internal corporate event, a few weeks may be sufficient. Larger conferences, product launches and formal corporate gatherings may require several months of preparation, depending on the venue, speakers, vendors and expected attendance.

What is the most important part of corporate event planning?

There is no single element that guarantees success. However, clear objectives, realistic budgeting, good organisation and effective communication are essential. Guest experience and event execution should also remain priorities.

What software can I use to manage corporate event registration?

You can use an event management platform such as AriyaHQ to manage digital invitations, guest registration, RSVP responses, bulk communication and QR code guest passes.

How do I manage guest check-in at a corporate event?

Prepare your guest list before the event, assign registration personnel, establish clear entry points and use a reliable verification process. QR code guest passes can also help make guest identification and entry more organised.

How do I measure the success of a corporate event?

Measure the event against its original objectives. Useful indicators include registrations, actual attendance, attendee feedback, budget performance, business enquiries, networking outcomes and post-event engagement.

title: Guest Management Software: How to Organise and Manage Your Event Guest List
excerpt: Learn how to keep one reliable event guest list, track invitations and RSVPs, coordinate follow-ups and protect guest information.

content:
Introduction

An event guest list can start as a few names in a notebook and quickly become a mix of spreadsheets, chats, invitation drafts and last-minute updates. When nobody knows which copy is current, organisers can miss replies, send duplicate invitations or plan around the wrong headcount.

Guest management software gives an event team a central way to organise invitees and track the steps from invitation to attendance. The right setup should make coordination easier without collecting more personal information than the event needs.

What guest management software should help you do

A useful guest-management process keeps each person's essential event details together: their name, contact method, invitation status, RSVP and any event-specific notes the team genuinely needs. For a wedding or a family celebration, that might include which ceremony a guest is invited to. For a conference, it could include an attendee group or registration status.

Some platforms also support invitations, RSVP collection, reminders and check-in. Features vary, so confirm which steps a particular product supports before relying on it on event day. A guest list is not automatically a ticket-validation system.

Build one reliable guest list

Start with a single agreed list and decide who is responsible for keeping it current. If several people are contributing names, set a clear process for adding, correcting and removing entries. Use consistent labels for groups such as family, speakers, staff or invited guests rather than creating slightly different categories in separate files.

Collect only fields that serve a clear purpose. A name and invitation status may be enough for a small gathering; a larger event may also need a contact detail and RSVP. If plus-ones are allowed, record the allocation explicitly so the guest and the team have the same expectation.

Track invitations and RSVPs consistently

Choose a small set of statuses and use them the same way: not yet invited, invitation sent, attending, unable to attend and follow-up needed. Record the date an invitation was sent and the latest response so another organiser can pick up the task without searching through personal chats.

Set an RSVP deadline that leaves time to confirm venue arrangements, catering and seating. Follow up politely with non-responders, then update the list when plans change. An RSVP is an indication of intent, not a guarantee that someone will attend, so keep a practical buffer for uncertainty.

Plan guest communication

Make every invitation easy to understand. Include the event date, location, response instructions and deadline; share travel or access information when it is relevant. Send reminders only when they help guests act, and make corrections clear if the schedule or venue changes.

Before sending a bulk message, check the recipient group, proofread the details and consider whether recipients can see one another's addresses. Avoid sending repeated messages through several channels unless there is a good reason. Keep a record of important updates so the event team knows what guests have been told.

Protect guest information

Guest lists contain personal information. Limit access to the people who need it, use a secure account or storage location, and avoid posting attendee names, phone numbers, dietary details or QR passes in public channels. Do not collect sensitive details unless they are necessary and you have a clear plan for handling them.

Agree when old lists and exports should be deleted. If a spreadsheet is shared, check its permissions and remove access when a person no longer needs it. These simple practices help reduce accidental disclosure while keeping the team organised.

Choose a process that fits the event

A spreadsheet can work well for a small event when one person owns updates and the list is not being copied into several places. As the guest count or planning team grows, a dedicated tool may make invitations, responses and follow-ups easier to coordinate. Compare the features you will actually use, how guests respond, who can access the information and whether the process works on mobile.

For weddings, AriyaHQ provides event-planning features for managing invitations and guest responses. See the Ariya wedding RSVP and guest-management guide for the current product details, then confirm that the available options fit your event before you send invitations.

A practical final check

Before invitations go out, confirm that the list is up to date, the event details are correct, each guest has the right allocation and the RSVP deadline is visible. Decide who will monitor replies, how corrections will be communicated and who can access the list. Before event day, export or prepare only the information the team needs and keep it secure.

A clear process matters more than a complicated tool. Start with one source of truth, make responsibilities explicit and choose software only when it solves a real coordination problem.

title: How to Plan Event Check-in and Manage Guest Arrivals at an Event
excerpt: Plan event check-in, assign staff, reduce queues, verify guests and prepare for common arrival problems.
imageAlt: Event guest access card prepared for check-in
author: Ariya Journal
content:
Introduction

Long queues, missing names, unapproved guests, slow registration and confusion at the entrance are common problems at conferences, weddings, product launches, seminars and other large gatherings.

These problems are not always caused by the number of attendees. Often, they happen because the organiser has not properly planned how guests will arrive, be identified and gain entry.

A successful event check-in process should make it easy for invited guests to enter while helping organisers maintain control over attendance.

In this guide, we'll explain how to plan event check-in, organise registration staff, manage guest arrivals and handle common entry problems.

We'll also explain how an event management platform such as AriyaHQ can help organisers prepare guest lists, issue unique QR code guest passes and manage guest entry more efficiently.

What Is Event Check-in?

Event check-in is the process of identifying guests when they arrive at an event and recording or confirming their attendance.

Depending on the event, this may involve checking a guest's name against a registration list, confirming their registration details, scanning a QR code guest pass or directing them to the appropriate entrance.

A typical event check-in process involves:

  1. Guest arrives at the venue.
  2. Guest approaches the registration desk or entry point.
  3. Registration staff identify the guest.
  4. The guest's invitation or registration is verified.
  5. Attendance is recorded or confirmed.
  6. The guest is directed into the event.

The process may look simple, but it requires preparation, especially when hundreds or thousands of people are expected.

Why Event Check-in Needs Proper Planning

Without a clear entry process, even a well-organised event can experience unnecessary delays.

Here are some reasons to plan check-in before event day.

Reduce long queues: Having enough registration staff and clearly defined entry points helps prevent guests from waiting unnecessarily.

Improve guest experience: Guests should be able to arrive, confirm their attendance and enter without confusion.

Maintain attendance records: Organisers need to know who has arrived, particularly for events with limited capacity or controlled access.

Prevent unauthorised entry: A proper verification process helps staff distinguish registered guests from people who are not on the approved list.

Manage different guest categories: VIPs, speakers, staff, sponsors and general attendees may need different entry arrangements.

Avoid last-minute confusion: A documented process gives registration staff clear instructions on what to do when problems occur.

Step 1: Finalise Your Guest and Registration List

Your check-in process should begin with an accurate guest list.

Before the event, review your registration records and ensure that the information available to your team is current.

Your guest list should ideally include:

  • Guest's full name.
  • Registration or invitation reference.
  • Phone number, where needed for identification.
  • Guest category.
  • Number of approved attendees.
  • Special access or seating instructions, where applicable.

For larger events, organise the list into useful categories.

For example:

  • General attendees: main registration desk.
  • VIP guests: dedicated VIP desk.
  • Speakers: speaker reception point.
  • Sponsors: sponsor registration point.
  • Event staff: staff check-in point.
  • Media representatives: media registration point.

Where AriyaHQ fits in: AriyaHQ helps organisers manage guest information, digital invitations, registrations and unique QR code guest passes. Preparing guest information ahead of time makes it easier for the event team to organise the arrival process.

Step 2: Estimate Your Expected Arrival Volume

One of the biggest mistakes organisers make is planning check-in based only on the total number of registered guests.

What matters is not just how many people are attending, but how many are likely to arrive within the same period.

For example, an event with 500 registered attendees may not have a problem if guests arrive steadily over three hours. However, if 300 people arrive within the first 30 minutes, the registration process needs to handle a much higher volume.

Consider the following:

  • Total expected attendees.
  • Event start time.
  • Registration opening time.
  • Expected peak arrival period.
  • Number of entry points.
  • Average time required to verify each guest.

A simple check-in capacity example

Suppose your event expects 300 guests to arrive within the first hour.

If one registration staff member takes an average of 30 seconds to verify a guest, that person can process approximately two guests per minute.

In theory:

  • One staff member: 120 guests per hour.
  • Two staff members: 240 guests per hour.
  • Three staff members: 360 guests per hour.

These are theoretical figures. Real check-in takes longer when guests need help finding their details, resolving registration issues or asking questions.

For this reason, plan some additional capacity rather than working with the theoretical maximum.

Step 3: Choose the Right Check-in Method

The best check-in method depends on your event size, guest type, available technology and entry requirements.

Here are three common approaches.

Manual name-list check-in

With manual check-in, registration staff use a printed guest list or spreadsheet to find each attendee's name and confirm their entry.

Advantages:

  • Simple to organise.
  • Does not require every guest to have a digital pass.
  • Can be useful for small gatherings.

Limitations:

  • Searching through long lists can take time.
  • Multiple registration desks need updated copies.
  • Recording attendance manually can create errors.
  • Printed lists may become outdated when registrations change.

This method can work for smaller events, but it becomes harder to manage as the guest list grows.

Digital registration check-in

Digital check-in uses an electronic guest list or registration system to help staff find and verify attendees.

Advantages:

  • Guest information can be organised digitally.
  • Changes can be easier to manage.
  • Attendance records can be maintained electronically, depending on the system.
  • Staff can work with structured registration information.

Limitations:

  • Staff need to understand the system.
  • Devices and internet connectivity may be required, depending on the setup.
  • A backup process is still important.

QR code guest-pass check-in

If you use QR guest passes, test the scanning process and prepare a manual fallback for passes that cannot be read. For more on preparing QR passes, see our QR code event-ticket guide.

Step 4: Design Your Registration Area

Your registration area should be easy to locate and should not obstruct the main entrance.

When planning the layout, consider the movement of guests from the venue entrance to the registration desk and then into the event space.

A practical layout may include:

  • A welcome or direction point.
  • General guest registration desks.
  • VIP registration desk.
  • Speaker and special guest reception.
  • An issue-resolution desk.
  • An entry point into the event hall.

For events with large attendance, separate queues can make a significant difference.

Use visible signs to tell guests where to go. For example:

  • General Registration.
  • VIP Registration.
  • Speakers and Guests.
  • Media Registration.
  • Event Staff.

Avoid placing all registration activities at one small table near a narrow entrance.

Also ensure that guests who have completed check-in can move away from the registration area without blocking people who are still waiting.

Step 5: Determine How Many Registration Staff You Need

Your registration team should be large enough to manage expected arrivals without creating unnecessary queues.

The number of staff required depends on:

  • Expected attendance.
  • Arrival patterns.
  • Check-in method.
  • Number of guest categories.
  • Complexity of guest verification.
  • Whether additional guest enquiries are expected.

For a small event, two or three people may be sufficient.

For a larger event, you may need separate teams for general registration, VIP guests, issue resolution and guest direction.

A useful staffing structure is:

  • Registration supervisor: oversees check-in.
  • Registration officers: verify guest details and record arrivals.
  • VIP reception officers: welcome and assist VIP guests.
  • Guest support officers: resolve missing registration details.
  • Ushers: direct guests to seating and event areas.
  • Queue managers: organise guest movement and reduce congestion.

Step 6: Prepare for Common Guest Check-in Problems

Even with careful planning, some guests will arrive with problems.

Your team should know how to respond without creating unnecessary delays.

Guest's name is missing from the list

This may happen because of a spelling difference, an outdated guest list or a registration that was not completed.

What to do:

  • Ask for the guest's registration details.
  • Check alternative name spellings.
  • Verify the information with the event coordinator where necessary.
  • Use a designated issue-resolution process rather than holding up the main queue.

Guest arrives without a QR code

Some guests may delete their invitation, lose access to their email or arrive without their phone.

What to do:

  • Search for the guest using their name or another approved identifier.
  • Confirm the invitation or registration details.
  • Follow the organiser's procedure for issuing or confirming access.

Do not automatically allow entry simply because someone claims to have received an invitation.

Guest brings an additional person

An attendee may arrive with a partner, friend or colleague who was not included in the original registration.

What to do:

  • Check the number of approved attendees associated with the invitation.
  • Refer the request to the designated supervisor if additional access is being considered.
  • Record any approved changes.

Guest arrives late

Late arrivals are common, particularly in cities where traffic can be unpredictable.

What to do:

  • Keep the registration process available for the agreed arrival period.
  • Ensure someone can assist late guests.
  • Provide directions to the appropriate seating or event area.
  • Make sure late arrivals do not interrupt an ongoing programme.

Guest presents a pass that cannot be verified

A pass may be unclear, damaged, inaccessible or not recognised by the check-in system.

What to do:

  • Ask the guest for alternative registration details.
  • Check the approved guest list.
  • Refer unresolved cases to the registration supervisor.
  • Follow the event's access policy.

A clear escalation process helps staff make consistent decisions.

Step 7: Plan for Late Arrivals and Unexpected Guests

Your registration process should not stop working once the main arrival period has passed.

Some guests may arrive after the event has started, while others may arrive without completing the expected registration process.

Plan for these situations in advance.

For late arrivals:

  • Keep at least one registration officer available.
  • Make sure late guests know where to enter.
  • Have ushers ready to guide them quietly into the event.

For unexpected guests:

  • Establish who has authority to approve additional entry.
  • Set a process for checking available capacity.
  • Record any approved additions.
  • Avoid allowing registration staff to make independent exceptions without guidance.

This is particularly important for corporate events, conferences and ticketed gatherings where venue capacity and access control matter.

Step 8: Brief and Train Your Registration Team

Do not wait until guests begin arriving before explaining how check-in should work.

Hold a briefing before the event and walk the team through the process.

Every registration officer should understand:

  1. Where they are assigned.
  2. Which guest category they are handling.
  3. How to verify a guest.
  4. How to confirm attendance.
  5. What to do when a name is missing.
  6. How to handle additional guests.
  7. Who to contact when a problem cannot be resolved.

Where possible, conduct a test before the event.

Ask team members to practise checking in sample guests so they understand the process before working with actual attendees.

Step 9: Test Your Equipment and Backup Arrangements

A digital check-in process depends on more than having a laptop or phone available.

Before the event, confirm that:

  • Devices are charged.
  • Chargers and power banks are available.
  • Internet connectivity has been tested where required.
  • Registration links or systems can be accessed.
  • QR code scanning equipment is working, where applicable.
  • Staff know how to access the guest information they need.
  • A backup guest list or alternative verification procedure is available.

For venues with unreliable connectivity, discuss the available offline or alternative access arrangements with your platform provider before event day. Do not assume that a system supports offline check-in without confirming it.

Step 10: Monitor Guest Arrivals During the Event

Once check-in begins, the registration supervisor should monitor how the process is performing.

Pay attention to:

  • Queue length.
  • Average waiting time.
  • Number of guests who have arrived.
  • Number of guests still expected.
  • Registration issues.
  • VIP and speaker arrivals.
  • Any entry bottlenecks.

If one registration desk becomes overwhelmed, consider redirecting guests to another available desk.

Maintain communication between the registration team, ushers and event coordinator.

A check-in process should be flexible enough to respond to changing arrival patterns.

Event Check-in Day Checklist
